findings.summary: Spec P6 is structurally unmet. Both P6 tests inject opts.triageSpawnRuntime, which per runChannelWrite takes the injection branch (deps.spawnTriage ?? ... returns the injected-runtime path) and skips the production-assembled default runtime. The test's readResult is a self-built copy calling readTriageResult, which the spec explicitly disqualifies ('⛔ 自建 runtime 注入的用例不算数'). The production default readResult at tick-run.ts:1521-1530 (30×1s retry + loud failure naming runId via readTriageResult) has zero test coverage. As a result P1–P3 (discriminant / loud failure / empty-vs-missing) are only evidenced against a test-local duplicate, never against the actual production-assembled deps — leaving open the exact regression class this package exists to prevent. To satisfy P6, add a test that calls runChannelWrite WITHOUT opts.spawnTriage and WITHOUT opts.triageSpawnRuntime (so the default branch at tick-run.ts:1506-1531 builds the runtime), with a fake bus where dr-triage.result.v1 appears only after spawn, and assert casCount === decisions and that board:agent-runs is re-read post-spawn.

Dev-note records the wrong input_commit. Spec §5 item 4 requires the dev-note input_commit to be the dispatch's input_commit for this attempt, not an unrelated commit. The dispatch input_commit is be623c20827f74af6062332381e4e47d9bc2277b, but docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_g5_triage_read_01.md:4 records 8a087696e3db288a583f0e02d8b4cb34614f2362 — a different hash. This breaks the audit trail and the spec's identity discipline.
